blocks.x: Our business uses AI tools to help draft written work. This page explains what that means for you. It takes two minutes to read and it applies to everyone.

x: Tidying up field notes into a clear job record.
Drafting estimates, scopes of work and customer messages.
Writing down procedures that currently only exist in someone's head.
Sorting voicemails and emails into a priority order.

blocks.x: What AI is never used for

AI does not set prices. AI does not decide whether something meets code. AI does not decide whether a permit is needed. AI does not make safety decisions. AI does not replace the judgement of a licensed person. If an AI tool gives you an answer on any of these, ignore it and ask a qualified person.
What you must never put into an AI tool

x: Customer payment details, card numbers or bank information.
Government identification numbers or dates of birth.
Employee records, disciplinary matters or pay information.
Confidential business documents, supplier agreements or anything marked confidential.
Photographs showing a customer's home interior, documents or personal belongings.

blocks.x: Where you need to use a customer's name or address to get useful output, use the minimum necessary and nothing more.
Your responsibility before anything is sent

x: Read every word of the AI output. Do not skim it.
Check it against the source — the technician's note, the job record, the written warranty.
Run it through the Quality-Control Checklist.
Correct anything wrong. If you cannot verify something, remove it or ask.
If it touches gas, electrical hazard, water damage, injury, a customer alleging damage, code, permits, or work outside our licence — stop and escalate.

blocks.x: AI writes a first draft. You are responsible for what goes out. If you would not put your own name to it, do not send it.

I have read and understood this summary. I understand that I remain responsible for reviewing and verifying any AI-assisted output before it is sent, filed or acted upon, and that I must escalate rather than guess.
